features.name: Run records that attach to the right feature and show gate runs
features.description: feat-068 and feat-069 got a wrong or missing run summary because session-clean ran before the completion commit existed: the feature step said 'not completed' and the run step still wrote a record nobody claimed. Report that case under its own status, do not write the stray record, record how many gate runs fell in a window, correct the two summaries from their real records, and put the order in AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: a completed feature whose completion is not committed reports 'completion not committed', not 'not completed', and a feature that is not completed still reports 'not completed'
session-clean.sh prints a loud warning for uncommitted completions and writes no run-telemetry record in that case
each run record carries gate_runs (count, passed, failed, failed gate names) from a log that harness-verify.sh appends to, measured when the log exists and missing otherwise
the feat-068 and feat-069 summaries are rebuilt from their real records with summary_from_record, no numbers typed by hand
AGENTS.md End of Session gives the order: commit the completion, run session-clean.sh, commit the telemetry files
an outside-agent review of the install-script changes from feat-068 is run, or its absence is stated in the evidence
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file
features.verification: python3 -m pytest tests/test_feature_run_record.py tests/test_run_telemetry.py -q && bash scripts/harness-verify.sh
features.evidence: Failing tests first, then code: tests/test_feature_run_record.py (2 new), tests/test_run_telemetry.py (3 new, gate_runs), scripts/tests/test_session_clean.sh (2 new), scripts/tests/test_harness_verify.sh (2 new); 180 pytest and all shell tests pass, mypy clean, harness-verify.sh passed all 11 gates with output saved to a file. A completion not yet committed now reports 'completion not committed' and session-clean.sh warns and writes no run record; harness-verify.sh appends one line per run to ~/.agent-skills-setup/state/harness-verify-runs.jsonl and each run record carries gate_runs (count, passed, failed, failed gate names). feat-068 and feat-069 summaries were rebuilt from their real records with summary_from_record (feat-068: 5097 output tokens, 15.3e6 ms wall; feat-069: 1669, 1.99e6 ms); the stray records 57f13686b4, f9dc9c7a13 and cb5536ef29 stay in docs/telemetry/runs as unclaimed. AGENTS.md End of Session now gives the order. A new test found that harness/guards/tests/test_stop_verify.sh ran the real harness-verify.sh against the caller's HOME and wrote 4 fake gate runs per run-tests.sh call; it now uses a temp report path. Outside review of feat-068 (codex-kiro) gave 3 findings, none introduced by it: setup-host.sh overwrites a foreign AGY statusLine and install_statusline leaves stack_with_default alone when the statusLine is foreign (both as before feat-068), and the refresh path has no Python fallback without jq (also as before; the statusline script itself needs jq and renders nothing without it). Not fixed, queued. Review by a fresh-context subagent (no outside model; the change is telemetry and test plumbing, not hooks or permissions) found 5 points; 4 reproduced and fixed with a failing test first (a1683a1): (1) an unwritable state dir printed a redirect error from the new log append, so console output changed; (2) feature_run_record.py ignored HARNESS_VERIFY_LAST_REPORT while harness-verify.sh and session-clean.sh honored it; (3) an empty HARNESS_VERIFY_LAST_REPORT meant 'keep nothing' in harness-verify.sh but fell back to the real log in session-clean.sh; (4) session-clean.sh matched the phrase 'completion not committed' anywhere in the output, now only a status line ending in it. Also found by running the close in the new order: the feature record built its own run record without the gate runs log, so gate_runs was missing from feat-070's record; fixed with a failing test first (ea4bb74). Not fixed: a completed feature in a repo where git fails or feature_list.json is untracked reports 'completion not committed' (true in the sense that no commit shows it, but the cause is not named); harness-verify-runs.jsonl is never rotated and is read whole for each record (about 1 line per gate run); every session-clean.sh run writes one small tail record that no feature claims; the order (commit, then session-clean) is a warning and a rule in AGENTS.md, not a block.

features.name: AGY stack_with_default: AGY ignores it at the top level and drops a false value; setup-host keeps a foreign statusLine
features.description: A live probe showed AGY reads stack_with_default only inside the statusLine object; the installer and setup-host.sh wrote it at the top level, where AGY ignores it, so the 'stop stacking' part of feat-068 changed nothing. Write it as false inside statusLine, remove the inert top-level key we wrote, correct the feat-068 evidence, and stop setup-host.sh from replacing a foreign AGY statusLine.
acceptance_criteria: install_statusline for gemini leaves stack_with_default out of settings.json on a fresh file, on a jq merge, on the refresh of our own script, and on the python fallback, and removes the top-level and the nested key if present
no other key in settings.json changes, and a foreign statusLine stays untouched by install_statusline and by setup-host.sh
a live agy session with the installed settings shows only our line (no native '? for shortcuts' line)
the feat-068 evidence no longer claims the installer turned stacking off
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file
features.evidence: Live probes in agy under tmux (160 cols): top-level stack_with_default true shows only our line; nested statusLine.stack_with_default true shows AGY's native line ('? for shortcuts', model) above ours; neither shows only ours. So the key must sit inside statusLine, and feat-068's top-level write never did anything. A first attempt wrote nested false; the installed file was clean right after install.sh but agy rewrote settings.json within about 20 s of a running session and removed the false (omitempty). The installer therefore writes no key at all, which is what 'off' means to AGY, and removes both the top-level and a nested true. scripts/tests/test_statusline_command.sh 38 passed (failed first: 4, then 5 after the rule changed): fresh, jq merge, refresh, old top-level true, nested true, python fallback without jq, foreign AGY statusLine left alone by install_statusline and by setup-host.sh (run against a throwaway HOME with closed stdin; the first version of that test hung on setup-host's ntfy prompt and was killed, real settings untouched). setup-host.sh now skips an AGY settings.json whose statusLine is not ours. harness-verify.sh passed all 11 gates with output saved to a file. feat-068's evidence carries a correction. Not done: no outside-model review (install-script change, one codex-kiro pass was run on feat-068 and its findings drove this); before the first message agy sends a payload the script shows only the left part of the line (unverified why, probably no context_window_size yet); the cause of the row sometimes sitting higher is still unknown and not reproduced; the Claude-side install paths are unchanged.

features.name: AGY statusline: show the 5-hour limit of the current model's family, not the lowest across families
features.description: The statusline showed the lowest *-5h bucket in agy's payload. agy keeps two separate 5-hour limits (Gemini models and Claude/GPT models, the payload's 3p-5h), so on a Gemini session with 59% left it showed '5h 0%' whenever the Claude/GPT limit was used up. Pick the bucket by model family and fall back to the lowest only when that bucket is missing.
acceptance_criteria: a model name starting with 'Gemini' shows the gemini-5h remaining percentage even when 3p-5h is lower

a model name starting with 'Claude' or 'GPT' shows the 3p-5h remaining percentage even when gemini-5h is lower; a name that is none of Gemini, Claude or GPT shows the lowest *-5h bucket, because the 3p mapping is not confirmed for other names
if the chosen bucket is missing, or the model name is empty, the lowest *-5h bucket is shown as before
a payload without quota (Claude Code) still renders cwd and context, and a malformed quota never blanks the line
the width, EOF and Claude Code cases in test_statusline_command.sh still pass
all 11 harness gates pass, with gate output saved to a file
features.evidence: Found by capturing every statusline call in live agy: the line showed '5h 0%' on a Gemini session that agy's own /quota reported at 59% five-hour remaining, because the script took the lowest *-5h bucket and agy keeps a separate Claude/GPT limit (payload 3p-5h) that was used up; it had looked right earlier only because 3p-5h happened to be full. The line now shows the model family's own bucket (Gemini -> gemini-5h, Claude/GPT -> 3p-5h, any other name or missing bucket -> lowest). After install, live agy showed 5h 57% while agy -p /quota showed Gemini five-hour remaining 57%; run time 65 ms. scripts/test_statusline_command.sh 49 passed (failed first: 4, then 4 after the review). A fresh subagent found remaining_fraction was not range-checked (-0.5 printed '5h -50%', 1.5 printed '5h 150%', and an out-of-range own bucket hid a valid fallback) and, as a pre-existing case, a non-object model blanked the whole line; both fixed with failing tests first. harness-verify.sh passed all 11 gates with output saved to a file. Also learned: before the first message agy's first payloads have agent_state authenticating, context_window_size 0 and no quota, so the line shows only [model] cwd git:(branch) for about 4 s (12 s once, cause not found); the script takes 60-90 ms per call and is not the cause. Not done: the 3p-5h mapping for Claude and GPT names is a guess, since agy -p /model lists only the current model and no Claude or GPT display name was seen; the model's own weekly limit (agy shows 'Gemini 4 Argon Weekly Limit 0%') is not displayed; the 12 s startup case and the occasional higher row are unexplained.
